note: testOps() exercises ecMulGen(1), ecOnCurve, ecNegate, ecMul(g, 2n), ecMul(g, 0n), ecAdd(g, g), ecPointX/Y, ecMakePoint and ecEncodeCompressed. It takes NO arguments and needs no cryptographic witness, so the fixture's ACTUAL compiled locking script runs end-to-end on @bsv/sdk's Spend engine — the same thing the live regtest node did when it rejected this fixture with 'Script failed an OP_VERIFY operation'. It failed on two degenerate EC cases the codegen never handled: ecAdd(P,P) could not double (fixed in 8a6494b4) and ecMul(P,2n) returned the all-zero point (fixed here). This spec is the standing proof that both are gone. It also now pins the THIRD degenerate case, P + (-P): that is the point at infinity, which affine x||y cannot encode, so ecAdd returns the all-zero blob from a SUCCESSFUL script — the same thing ecMul yields for any k = 0 (mod n). The return value alone cannot be distinguished from a real point; ecOnCurve is the only detector, and `assert(!ecOnCurve(ecAdd(g, neg)))` pins that it works, in every tier and every format. Selecting the tangent on (px == qx) alone answered this with 2G — on-curve, plausible, wrong, and accepted by the same gate. ecAdd(g, neg) is used rather than ecMul(g, 0n) because the two produce the same all-zero point while ecAdd costs ~26 KB of script against ecMul's ~429 KB, which would have grown this fixture 94% for no extra property.
acceptOnlyReason: testOps() takes no arguments and reads no caller-controlled value — every assertion is a fixed EC identity over the generator — so there is no input to vary and no reject spend is constructible for this fixture. The negative direction is covered instead by packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/ec-mul-k2.test.ts, which compares the emitted primitives against @bsv/sdk's own secp256k1 for a spread of scalars, and by the p256/p384-primitives specs, which do carry a reject.

spends.note: every EC assertion in testOps() holds on the real Spend engine, including the ecMul(g,2n) and ecAdd(g,g) doubling cases that used to make this script unspendable

goldenHashesNote: R-052 / CL-BUG-095 (no length validation on any Point argument in any tier) and R-053 / CL-BUG-096 (ecAdd(P, O) returned an off-curve blob while the always-on EC optimizer rewrote the same expression as the identity) both moved this golden. The pin is deliberately self-invalidating: any later change to expected-script.hex must come back through this witness, whose spends re-EXECUTE the fixture's actual compiled locking script on the real @bsv/sdk Spend engine with real secp256k1 — which is why this fixture takes provenance path (A) rather than an allowlist hash. Both defects were reproduced by EXECUTION before the fix, not inferred: ecOnCurve(G||0xff) returned TRUE, ecPointX on a 32-byte blob succeeded, ecEncodeCompressed(G||0x01) flipped the compressed sign from 02 to 03, and ecAdd(G, allZero64) returned cf88213f...169139c6 with ecOnCurve(result) false. All seven independently written compilers regenerate these exact bytes; before each regeneration the conformance run reported 0 mismatches BETWEEN compilers against 70 unanimous golden mismatches, which is the signature of a correct port meeting a stale reference rather than a port bug. expected-ir.json is provably unmoved in both commits, so the ANF is untouched and only stack lowering changed.
